provenance.paper_title: Flash-VStream: Efficient Real-Time Understanding for Long Video Streams
supersedes_or_extends: Flash-VStream: Memory-Based Real-Time Understanding for Long Video Streams (arXiv:2406.08085)

evidence.paraphrase: A fixed-capacity context memory stores low-resolution visual-feature cluster centroids and temporal positions.
High-resolution visual features nearest to high-density context clusters are retained for detailed spatial augmentation and jointly activated in the language model.

A fixed K-means update incorporates each incoming low-resolution frame feature while maintaining a bounded centroid set. For Flash-VStream, this specifically supports fixed-rule insertion or replacement of Context Synopsis Memory.

Semantically similar frames are consolidated into cluster centroids to remove temporal redundancy. For Flash-VStream, this specifically supports merging or deduplication of overlapping entries of Context Synopsis Memory.

derived.hybrid_relation: Both memory levels store modality-native visual features; their multi-tier organization alone is not cross-representation hybrid memory.

adjudication_notes: Strict-tier full-paper review (PDF p. 3): During inference, the operative memory component (Context Synopsis Memory) changes through fixed-rule insertion or replacement, merging or deduplication of overlapping entries; the governing policy remains fixed, and any learning reported by the paper occurs before deployment. Training-time learning, when present, was not counted as T3.
